title: Coach Jackie J implores Netflix to address access for sports bars ahead of women’s World Cup
content:
The 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup figures to be one of the top sports stories of the year, with a more level playing field among the best teams and the USWNT hungry to avenge their early exit in 2023.

The Women’s World Cup will also be an experiment to see whether Netflix can successfully broadcast a big live sports tournament. The streamer has exclusive broadcast rights to the World Cup in the U.S. and Canada. Previously, Fox had the rights to the tournament, making accessibility a pretty easy question to answer — games would be available to watch on Fox and its affiliated channels. Streaming is a bit of a different beast.

Looking ahead to the event, breakout women’s sports personality Coach Jackie J is calling on Netflix to expand access to the games. So far, Netflix has not developed a plan to make the World Cup available in bars, restaurants and other commercial establishments — a common problem as streamers air more sports, and one that could hamper the momentum coming off the World Cup we just had in North America last summer.

“I have heard from owners of sports bars across the country, multiple different people messaging me, saying they’re worried they won’t be able to host any watch parties for one of the biggest women’s sports events of all time,” Coach Jackie said this week on her podcast, Is She Game? “Why? Because Netflix has the sole rights to the Women’s World Cup in 2027, and they’re a subscription service. And that is technically unavailable to commercial establishments. There’s no commercial licensing situation set up right now.”

Technically, it is illegal for bar or restaurant owners to show games through a personal streaming login. Companies like EverPass Media work as intermediaries, striking deals with streamers and then charging restaurant owners to air streaming games legally in their buildings. Some streamers offer standalone subscriptions for businesses. These commercial subscriptions can cost hundreds per month, on top of traditional cable. But businesses can be fined thousands if they show games illegally.

The problem has already cropped up as Prime Video and Peacock bought exclusive rights to big sporting events like NFL playoff games in recent years. Netflix’s ownership of the World Cup will be among the most prominent case studies.

Coach Jackie is calling the problem out early to set a precedent that Netflix ought to be a good partner for a growing women’s sports property.

“You want people to watch this, I want people to watch your broadcast … but if the bars and the places where people come together, can’t watch it, then it’s not going to hit the mark,” she said.

“Think about it, if the women’s sports bars who care the most about this, are the most proactive in figuring out how to get it on TV, if they’re not able to get it on TV, you think the normie bars are going to be pulling it up on Netflix in their bar? No.

“Netflix needs to make it super accessible, and they need to make sure that if they do put out a commercial licensing fee, they need to make sure it’s not a bajillion dollars. Because women’s sports, we’ve already got a lot going on for us right now, we do not need an extra barrier to entry for the best tournament in sports.”

Women’s sports bars are seen as a key source of growth for the WNBA and other leagues. Businesses like the Sports Bra in Portland have built strong communities around airing women’s sports and hosting watch parties.

If Netflix wants to get in on more World Cup rights or larger NFL packages in the future, it must prove to its league partners and fans that its broadcasts will be accessible just as widely and easily as other sports can be found on Fox, CBS, or ESPN.

The Associated Press began its college football poll on Oct. 19, 1936, and it is now the longest-running poll of those that award national titles at the end of the season. The preseason poll was started in 1950.

title: Yankees Re-Sign Tim Hill To One-Year Deal
content:
The Yankees are bringing back a known quantity for their bullpen. Left-hander Tim Hill is returning on a one-year, $2.25MM deal, per ESPN’s Jeff Passan. The pact includes a $2.5MM club option for the 2028 season. Hill is a client of Paragon Sports International.

Hill, who will turn 37 in Spring Training, has pitched for the Yankees since midway through the 2024 season. The soft-tossing lefty is primarily a ground ball specialist. He has a 63.2% ground ball rate for his career, and since the start of 2024, over two-thirds of batted balls against Hill have been on the ground. That’s easily the best mark among qualified relievers in that span.

For the first two years of his Yankees tenure, Hill backed that up with solid run prevention. In 111 innings with New York from 2024-25, he delivered a 2.68 earned run average, held opposing hitters to a .604 OPS, and posted a sharp 5.7% walk rate. Hill’s 44.0% hard-hit rate in that time was not great, but thanks to the gaudy ground ball numbers, he did a good job of keeping the ball in the yard. He allowed only ten home runs in that span with New York, a rate of 0.81 homers per nine innings.

This past year was a different story. Hill led qualified relievers once again with a 68.8% ground ball rate, but his ERA shot up to 4.60 in 58 2/3 innings. Crucially, he allowed a dozen home runs, or a career-high rate of 1.84 HR/9. It was a strange mix of poor luck on the homers and good luck on other forms of contact. Opponents batted just .228 on balls in play off Hill, continuing a three-year trend of low BABIP values, and he also ranked in the 66th percentile by barrel rate (just 6.6%).

Under the surface, ERA estimators were split on Hill’s work. His 5.93 FIP suggested he was quite fortunate to post that 4.60 ERA, while his 3.66 SIERA was more favorable and right in line with last year’s 3.70 SIERA. However lucky Hill was (or wasn’t), the move is a low-cost reinforcement for the Yankees as they look to add to their bullpen this offseason.

title: Did Ole Miss Simply Lack The Grit To Get To Their Game On Time?
content:
On Friday, a nationwide ground stop lasting over four hours led to thousands of flight cancellations and delays from coast to coast. As a result, we're getting some Sunday afternoon college football, with No. 19 Ole Miss playing Oklahoma in Norman because they couldn't arrive on their previous schedule.

Per Ole Miss, who was flying out of Tupelo about 50 miles from their campus in Oxford, the ground stop began just a few minutes before the team buses were scheduled to leave for the airport, at 4 p.m. Once they learned that the stop would last for hours, the players were allowed to go, and they were called for a team meeting at 8 p.m., just a little before stop was lifted. Still, it was apparently too late for them to salvage their journey that night, and the SEC ultimately pushed the game back a day as a result.

"At that hour, due to the time required to rescreen the party and travel to the Tupelo airport, the crew's duty time would have expired prior to departure," the Ole Miss statement said. "There were no other flight options at that point, and we determined it was too late to put our student-athletes on a bus trip of eight or more hours. In addition, the flight crew's duty time restrictions prevented us from being able to fly out until Saturday afternoon at the earliest."

title: Robert Griffin III, Desmond Howard trade personal insults while arguing over Jeremiah Smith
content:
Desmond Howard and Robert Griffin III can’t stop bickering—nay, writing novel-sized excerpts to each other—on Twitter, and this is precisely why the “I Ain’t Reading All That” meme exists.

It all started when Howard, an analyst on ESPN’s College GameDay, delivered a hot take about Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith while appearing on First Take.

“When you talk about Jeremiah, it’s more than just losing [quarterback] Julian Sayin,” Howard said. “You’ve got to have those moments. In the last two years, give me one game where Jeremiah Smith, the wide receiver at Ohio State, was the difference in a big game in the last two years. This season and last season. Give me that game. As much as he puts up these magnificent numbers and these one-handed catches, I need moments against the top competition that makes me say ‘he was the guy.'”

Howard’s comments quickly made the rounds, especially because Howard won the Heisman while starring at Michigan in 1991, and Robert Griffin III emerged as Jeremiah Smith’s biggest fan—or Howard’s biggest hater, depending on how you look at it.

While serving as an analyst on Fox’s Big Noon Saturday broadcast of Ohio State’s 28-19 win over Northwestern on Saturday, Griffin addressed Howard’s criticism of Smith.

“When you talk about the Heisman Trophy, my guy Desmond Howard, he’s been very critical of Jeremiah Smith and said, ‘When does this guy ever show up in big-time games?'” Griffin said. “Well, he’s shown up in big-time games all over the place, and Desmond Howard has to stop hating on Jeremiah Smith just because he goes to Ohio State. That’s not the right way to do this, and we’ve got to be better in our Heisman brotherhood.”

Griffin, who won the Heisman as the Baylor quarterback before briefly starring in the NFL, then posted that clip alongside 353 additional words on X (formerly Twitter):

Jeremiah Smith is the FBS record holder for receiving yards for a player in his first 3 years in college.

You see Desmond Howard and anyone with eyes knows that Jeremiah Smith is ALWAYS THE DIFFERENCE on any field he steps on.

Jeremiah Smith is the best player in the Country, one of the greatest WRs we HAVE EVER SEEN in College Football History and an incredible young man who ALWAYS SHOWS UP.

The Heisman fraternity would be honored to welcome him into our family.

Desmond Howard is a legend, but even legends have to be checked. He needs to stop hating on Jeremiah Smith and recognize his greatness regardless of what school he went to.

— Robert Griffin III (@RGIII) November 14, 2026

Howard responded later Saturday night.

“Oh Robert, are you STILL on this app manufacturing Twitter beef for attention?” Howard wrote. “I thought you would have stopped doing that based on how it has worked out for you in the past. Oh well.

“Jeremiah Smith is an extraordinary talent. Nobody is questioning that. My point was whether he’s been THE difference-maker in Ohio State’s biggest games as a Heisman candidate. That’s a legitimate football discussion, not an attempt to discredit the young man based on the school he attends.

Brother.

Brother Desmond,

I didn’t challenge your opinion.
I destroyed it.

The problem is you are never being honest.

Not honest when it comes to Jeremiah Smith and don’t you think we forgot about CJ Stroud.

title: Phillies Interested In Jonathan Loaisiga
content:
Reports indicate that right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga is receiving widespread interest in free agency. The Dodgers were the most recent entrant into his market alongside the Yankees, Mets, and Blue Jays. It appears the Phillies have also entered the fray for Loaisiga’s services, as reported by Jon Heyman of the New York Post. That makes at least five known suitors for the 32-year-old reliever, whom MLBTR projects to earn a two-year, $13MM deal.

Loaisiga is coming off his best season in five years. Despite having a length injury history, including IL stints in every season from 2019-25, he finally stayed off the IL in 2026 and delivered 67 innings out of the Diamondbacks’ bullpen. That was a nice surprise considering Loaisiga entered Spring Training as a non-roster invitee. Even better, he delivered a stellar 2.42 earned run average, 56.4% ground ball rate, and 5.0% walk rate, making him one of Arizona’s best relievers and a key upside play for bullpen-needy clubs in free agency.

That Loaisiga managed a 67-inning total is impressive considering he combined for just 51 1/3 innings from 2023-25 with the Yankees. Since breaking out with a 2.17 ERA in 70 2/3 innings back in 2021, Loaisiga had missed time for shoulder inflammation, elbow inflammation, a torn UCL (which required season-ending surgery in April 2024), and mid-back tightness. From 2022-25, he had a 3.81 ERA in just under 100 innings with a subpar 9.4% K-BB rate but an excellent 55.5% ground ball rate.

There were a lot of positives in Loaisiga’s performance this year beyond the improved health. After working with slightly diminished velocity on his trademark sinker in 2025, he bumped it back up to 97.9 mph with the D-backs, which was right in line with his career norms. According to Statcast, Loaisiga ranked in the 92nd percentile or better by hard-hit rate (31.7%), chase rate (35.9%), barrel rate (3.5%), and average exit velocity (85.2 mph). Every one of his pitches had a positive run value, led by the four-seamer at +10 RV.

The Phillies ranked eighth in the Majors with 5.6 fWAR out of their relievers this year. Most of that came from flamethrowing closer Jhoan Duran, who earned 2.9 fWAR with a career-best 1.82 ERA and 31.4% K-BB rate in 61 appearances. Tim Mayza and Jonathan Bowlan were solid, but José Alvarado, Orion Kerkering, and Chase Shugart posted subpar run prevention and ground ball rates.

Loaisiga would solve both problems on a relatively inexpensive deal. As MLBTR’s Leo Morgenstern noted in our Offseason Outlook series, the Phillies could probably use three relievers but may focus more on bolstering the lineup, especially by adding starting-caliber outfielders. Our Payroll Tracker has the team at a $265MM cash payroll for 2027, leaving around $26.8MM to spend before they match last year’s total.

title: Pat McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit apologize to Wake Forest: ‘I don’t know what we were thinking’
content:
It only took one half of football for Pat McAfee and Kirk Herbstreit to admit they made a poor choice with their Wake Forest-SMU picks on College GameDay.

During Saturday’s edition of College GameDay in Boise, the ESPN college football analysts each picked SMU to beat No. 13 Wake Forest in Dallas.

https://t.co/AHZT24xpx3

— The Comeback NCAA (@TheComebackNCAA) November 15, 2026

“I don’t want to be one of those naysayers, and I love Coach Dickert, and I like Wake Forest,” McAfee said before turning the game prediction into a quick promo for College GameDay sponsor Coors Light.

“I’m going to watch SMU win this game,” McAfee added. “They are not ranked, but I like the SMU Mustangs to steal one here.”

Herbstreit then explained why he liked SMU to win the game.

“I said at the beginning of the show; Pat and I talked about this; it was like a chaos Saturday,” Herbstreit said. “I think there’s a lot of upsets up in the top-25. This is a great Wake Forest team. Thing is, SMU, since they joined the ACC, 12-0 at home in conference games. If you watched them last week, they put up 51 points. I just think they’re playing great football. Kevin Jennings, the difference in today’s game. They outscore Wake. And they’ll be ranked, finally, next week.”

Well, then the game started at 12 p.m. ET, and by halftime, Wake Forest had a 42-0 lead. The Demon Deacons would go on to win 49-7.

Fewer than two hours after College GameDay concluded, McAfee and Herbstreit delivered an apology to Wake Forest in a video posted to Herbstreit’s X account.

Herbstreit posted the following caption: “Whelp. Both [McAfee] and I want apologize from the bottom of our hearts for picking against [Wake Forest]. We thought SMU at home had a chance and BOY WE WE WRONG!! These boys are for real! Congrats and WE BELIEVE!”

Whelp. Both @PatMcAfeeShow and I want apologize from the bottom of our hearts for picking against @WakeFB
We thought SMU at home had a chance and BOY WE WE WRONG!!
These boys are for real!
Congrats and WE BELIEVE! https://t.co/CNBfE0X3LL

— Kirk Herbstreit (@KirkHerbstreit) November 14, 2026

“[Jake Dickert] was so good [as a guest on College GameDay] today; we should’ve known,” McAfee said in the video message alongside Herbstreit. “That’s on us.”

“That’s on us,” Herbstreit agreed.

“We apologize to Wake,” McAfee continued. “Wake is real.”

“We love Wake,” Herbstreit added.

“We think they’re so good,” McAfee said. “Like, I don’t know what we were thinking today.”

“What were we thinking?” Herbstreit asked. “I thought, you know, they’re on the road, SMU looked so good last week. I thought, ‘Maybe they’re in a spot to upset Wake.’ Boy, were we wrong.”

“SMU looked good last week,” McAfee responded. “You know who else did? Wake. Wake has looked good every week. We are sorry. That’s on us.”

“We’re sorry. We love Wake… We all love Wake,” Herbstreit reiterated.

Wake Forest improved to 9-1 with the blowout win and made an excellent case to move up in the next College Football Playoff rankings.

title: The Opener: Wilson, Bullpen Targets, AFL Award Winners
content:
The recently-retired Justin Verlander won his first of three career Cy Young awards on this day in 2011. Verlander fired off a career-high 251 innings in the regular season with a 2.40 earned run average, 250 strikeouts, four complete games, and an impressive 24-5 record. He was so dominant that year that he also won the AL MVP award a few days later, just the tenth time a pitcher won the Cy Young and MVP awards in the same year. Clayton Kershaw would become the eleventh such player in 2014.

1. A’s fielding calls from shortstop-needy teams

The Athletics are reportedly receiving trade interest in shortstop Jacob Wilson. There is no indication that the A’s are seriously looking to move him, so the interest could just be due diligence or fishing for a low-ball offer. Wilson, who underwent season-ending shoulder surgery in September, is entering the second season of a seven-year, $70MM extension inked back in January. In 80 games this year, he put up an 83 wRC+ while playing quality defense, as evidenced by his +9 Outs Above Average and +8 Fielding Run Value. A trade for Wilson would certainly be out of the box, though the interest is not surprising considering the state of the shortstop market in free agency. In MLBTR’s Top 50 Free Agents list, only Mauricio Dubón and J.P. Crawford are options at short, and they’re multi-positional types.

2. Dodgers, Yankees seeking bullpen upgrades

Big surprise. Almost every team is looking for quality relievers, and the Dodgers and Yankees are no different. The Dodgers are reportedly looking at Jonathan Loaisiga and Tim Hill. Loaisiga, who is coming off an excellent season for the Diamondbacks, is drawing interest from at least four teams and “getting closer” to signing a deal. At least five teams have known interest in Hill. As for the Yankees, general manager Brian Cashman calls upgrading the bullpen his “main priority” for the offseason. If they don’t manage to re-sign David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, and/or Hill, it’s possible the team could make a run at Adrian Morejon.

3. Arizona Fall League announces 2026 award winners

The Arizona Fall League just had its championship game yesterday, and with that, the league announced its award winners for the 2026 season. Among that group is Nationals pitching prospect Jarlin Susana, who won Pitcher of the Year. The 22-year-old right-hander was acquired from the Padres in the Juan Soto blockbuster back in August 2022. Susana reached Triple-A for the first time this year and currently rates as the No. 66 prospect in baseball, according to MLB Pipeline. He’s not on the Nats’ 40-man roster but could possibly debut for them in 2027.

title: Oklahoma AD Roger Denny fires back at SEC ‘carnival barker’ Paul Finebaum
content:
Along with disrupting travel nationwide, the FAA-issued ground stop has led to Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny and ESPN college football analyst Paul Finebaum trading barbs.

On Friday night, Denny released a statement blasting the decision made by Commissioner Greg Sankey and the SEC to move Oklahoma’s game vs. Ole Miss from Saturday to Sunday due to travel issues for Ole Miss.

https://t.co/6z039iPC1m

— Roger Denny (@Oklahoma_AD) November 14, 2026

And on Saturday morning’s edition of SEC Nation on SEC Network, Finebaum went off about Denny’s statement and defended the SEC and Ole Miss. Finebaum said that Denny was “pathetically pandering” to Oklahoma fans.

Paul Finebaum: “I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss… What I don’t think is correct is [Oklahoma AD Roger Denny] pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever…” https://t.co/k124Yv7Ocq

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 14, 2026

“I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss. But I believe the administration and Ole Miss did everything they could,” Finebaum said. “What I don’t think is correct is Roger Denny, the athletic director there, pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever, I don’t know.”

“Mr. Denny, the commissioner of the Southeastern Conference made a decision for the entire conference and for the safety of everyone,” Finebaum added. “He’s not concerned about what you’re doing with your fanbase. And what Roger Denny has been doing all this year is pandering to his fanbase.”

Well, later on Saturday, Denny responded to Finebaum’s comments during an in-studio appearance on On3’s Sooner Scoop.

Denny was asked, “Do you think this hurt [Oklahoma’s] relationship with [the SEC?]?”

He proceeded to refer to Finebaum as the SEC’s “carnival barker.”

Oklahoma AD Roger Denny went on with the @SoonerScoop crew and did not hold back. https://t.co/zJPQBgAzW4

— Andy Staples (@AndyStaples) November 14, 2026

“I don’t know. They’ll probably send their carnival barker out there to accuse me of pandering again,” Denny said. “And candidly, I don’t care. My job and my duty is to our players, our university, and our fanbase. If they don’t like the way we handle their business, I just don’t much care about that.”

And you can be sure that Finebaum, ESPN’s voice on all things SEC, will have a response to those comments in the coming days.

The Ole Miss-Oklahoma game was originally scheduled to kick off at 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday but was moved to 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. It will be televised on SEC Network, fittingly.

title: Latest On Ketel Marte
content:
Diamondbacks officials met with  Ketel Marte’s agent Charisse Espinosa-Dash during the GM Meetings this week, but the D’Backs “but did not seem to come away with a clear idea about what teams to which Marte would be willing to approve a deal,” the Arizona Republic’s Nick Piecoro writes.  Marte has full no-trade protection as a 10-and-5 player, so even though he is one of the offseason’s most prominent trade candidates, the possibility exists that Marte will remain in Arizona simply because he isn’t interested in changing teams.

It puts the D’Backs in something of an awkward position, especially since the impending lockout will interrupt all transactions activity for what could be months on end.  If Marte isn’t dealt by 10:59pm CT on December 1 (when the current collective bargaining agreement expires and the league is expected to lock out the players), the uncertainty over his future will continue to linger over all of the Diamondbacks’ remaining offseason plans.

As Piecoro puts it, “the Diamondbacks seem to have little choice but to sort of blindly attempt to make the best deal possible without knowing whether Marte will approve it.”  In terms of what that best deal might entail, Piecoro writes that the D’Backs have looked into all variety of trades in their early discussions about Marte — bringing in just prospects, swapping the second baseman for other established big league talents, or a trade package of both veteran and younger talent.

GM Mike Hazen naturally didn’t go into any detail about the Marte negotiations, but the executive expressed some regret at focusing on MLB-ready younger players in past trades of such star players as Zack Greinke or Paul Goldschmidt.  This could hint that Hazen is looking to add just the best talent available (whether that’s current big leaguers or longer-term prospects) while shopping Marte, which is probably a logical approach since Hazen’s options are already limited by Marte’s no-trade leverage.

One option still under consideration is moving Marte for another player on a hefty contract, for salary offset purposes.  The Diamondbacks “did not seem to be leaning in that direction,” as Piecoro says that Arizona’s preference would be to clear some of Marte’s remaining $91.75MM salary off the books and then reinvest that money into other roster needs.  That $91.75MM figure is a little higher than the $87.5MM owed to Marte in the initial terms of his contract, as Piecoro hears from a source that Marte unlocked incentive bonuses based on plate appearances.

The Blue Jays, Giants, Mariners, Phillies, Pirates, Rays, Red Sox, and Tigers all reportedly had some level of interest in Marte last offseason, and Toronto’s interest has continued into this winter.  As MLBTR’s Anthony Franco explored in a recent post about Marte’s potential market, Seattle, San Francisco, and Pittsburgh are probably out of the running based on various factors emerging within the last year.  There’s also the possibility that Marte’s infamous no-show of a game in Boston this past August might have put past suitors or any other teams off entirely.

title: Adalberto Mondesi Attempting Comeback
content:
Former Royals speedster Adalberto Mondesi is trying to get back to the majors, reports Will Sammon, Ken Rosenthal, and Katie Woo of The Athletic. Mondesi is currently playing winter ball in the Dominican Republic. His last big-league stint was in 2022.

Mondesi, 31, has appeared in three games with Aguilas. He’s 4-for-12 with two doubles and a triple so far. He also has four strikeouts. It’s the first live action for Mondesi in four years. He was most recently in Boston’s organization, but knee surgery cost him all of 2023. He was released at the end of the year and never latched on elsewhere.

At his peak, Mondesi was one of the biggest threats on the bases in the league. He stole 75 bases across 2018 and 2019, his first extended look as a big leaguer. He paced the league in triples in 2019. Mondesi led the majors with 24 steals in the shortened 2020 season.

The main drawback in Mondesi’s offensive profile was contact. He punched out at an alarming clip, particularly for a player lacking premier power. Mondesi has a 30.2% strikeout rate over 1,366 career plate appearances.

Mondesi spent time at second base, third base, and shortstop with the Royals. He had up-and-down results as a defender, but generally netted out as a neutral option at each spot. He’s played both second base and shortstop with Aguilas.

Mondesi is still relatively young. He’s a switch-hitter with some defensive versatility. The question would be whether the leg injuries have sapped his best skill. If he isn’t an elite base stealer, it’s hard to see him contributing enough to be worth an MLB roster spot, regardless of his contact issues.

title: Rex Ryan to appear on ESPN’s ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’ days after arrest
content:
ESPN analyst and former NFL head coach Rex Ryan turned himself in to authorities and was arrested in Nashville on Wednesday after allegedly running over the feet of two pedestrians with his pickup truck and leaving the scene earlier this month.

Just days later, it seems that Ryan will still appear on ESPN’s programming, including Sunday’s edition (10 a.m. ET) of the network’s NFL pregame show, Sunday NFL Countdown.

ESPN released a statement on Saturday night saying, “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.”

From an ESPN spokesperson on Rex Ryan:

“As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.”

Would not expect Ryan to address the matter on air.

— Richard Deitsch (@richarddeitsch) November 15, 2026

According to Nashville police, the pedestrians were crossing Broadway Street with a walk sign when Ryan turned right before “running over both victims’ feet,” along with “making contact with one of the individuals’ legs.”

Ryan allegedly kept driving, but the victims caught up to him at a red light. “They said he stepped out of the truck to argue with them, got back in, and drove away,” per the police statement.

The former head coach of the New York Jets (2009-14) and Buffalo Bills (2015-16) faces six misdemeanors: two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information/render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal.

After the news of Ryan’s arrest emerged on Wednesday, ESPN issued the following statement when reached by Awful Announcing for comment: “We are aware and are in touch with Rex.”

Ryan, 63, has been an analyst on ESPN since 2017 and stars on Sunday NFL Countdown alongside Mike Greenberg, Randy Moss, Alex Smith, Tedy Bruschi, and Adam Schefter. He’s also a frequent guest on ESPN’s Get Up.

The Yankees had the second-best bullpen ERA in the league last season. Maintaining that level will take some work this offseason, with several key pieces hitting free agency.

General manager Brian Cashman referred to the bullpen as New York’s “main priority” during an appearance on MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM this week (h/t Bryan Hoch of MLB.com).

Hoch adds that the Yankees are interested in bringing back two members of the 2026 relief corps, Tim Hill and Paul Blackburn. The team already issued a qualifying offer to closer David Bednar. The former Pirate excelled in his first full season as New York’s stopper and will likely reject the QO. Several teams are known to be in on Hill, including the Mets, Dodgers, Cardinals, Guardians, and Giants.

The club already re-upped with Blackburn once, retaining him on a one-year, $2MM deal last winter. Blackburn originally joined the organization in 2025 after he was cut by the Mets. He struggled in eight games to finish the season and came back on a cheap deal. Blackburn emerged as one of the most effective relievers in the league in 2026, compiling a 1.59 ERA over 85 frames.

[Related: How Paul Blackburn Became An Elite Reliever]

Blackburn ranked 41st on our Top 50 Free Agents list. We predict a two-year, $15MM deal. It’s not a massive price tag, but it’s certainly a step up from Blackburn’s last free agent agreement.

Here are a few other Yankees items…

  • If Bednar rejects the QO, left-hander Adrian Morejon could become a target, per Jorge Castillo of ESPN. The former Padre is the top option in the free agent reliever market. He’s expected to command a hefty contract, both in terms of money and years. Morejon tossed 86 innings with a 2.83 ERA and a 30.4% strikeout rate as the setup man ahead of Mason Miller this past season. There’s been rumblings about teams wanting to stretch him out as a starter, but he prefers to stay in the bullpen.

Dillon has been a hitting coach in the minors and majors for the past decade. He most recently worked for the Cubs’ Double-A affiliate.

The reverse could happen in New York, as Kuty mentions Espada as an option to take over Ausmus’ old role. Espada spent a few seasons as the Yankees’ third base coach in the mid-2010s under former manager Joe Girardi. Kris Bubic Drawing Widespread Interest
content:
While Tarik Skubal is getting the big headlines, another former Dodgers lefty is also drawing plenty of attention. Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic report that Kris Bubic is picking up interest “from contenders and non-contenders alike.”

Bubic has been slowed by arm injuries the past two seasons. His 2025 campaign was cut short by a rotator cuff strain. He made it through nine starts with the Royals to open this past season before going down with elbow soreness. Bubic began a rehab assignment in June, only to be shut down again with renewed elbow issues.

The Dodgers took a flyer on Bubic at the trade deadline, sending over a minor league pitcher in exchange for his services. Bubic made it back as a reliever during the final two weeks of the regular season. He put together five scoreless outings and made the club’s postseason roster. Bubic allowed runs in both of his playoff appearances, taking a loss in the NLDS and a blown save in the NLCS.

The 29-year-old Bubic debuted with Kansas City in 2020. He was a high draft pick and well-regarded prospect in the organization, but spent three seasons as a mediocre starter. Bubic had his 2023 almost entirely wiped out by Tommy John surgery. He returned as a reliever in 2024 and revived his career. The lefty posted a 2.67 ERA with an elite 32.2% strikeout rate in 27 games out of the Royals’ bullpen. Bubic reverted to the rotation in 2025 and delivered 20 starts of a 2.55 ERA and nearly a strikeout per inning.

The double-edged nature of Bubic’s profile brings a variety of suitors into play. A surefire playoff team could see him as a dice roll that could pay off handsomely with minimal investment. A non-playoff team could view him as a cheap route to a premier starter. As our guys put it in the Top 50 Free Agents list, “there aren’t many teams that don’t make sense as a landing spot.”

Bubic just made the cut for those rankings, slotting at No. 48. We predicted a one-year, $12.5MM deal. Bubic’s health would make a multi-year agreement a bit of a surprise, but a competitive market could encourage a needy team to go that route.

Jason Garrett pays heartfelt tribute to Dan Hicks on NBC’s Notre Dame broadcast
content:
The sports media world suffered a devastating loss with the sudden passing of beloved broadcaster Dan Hicks this week at the age of 64. Hicks delivered a remarkable career as a play-by-play broadcaster, headlined by 35 years as a versatile voice for NBC Sports, which included iconic calls in golf and the Olympics.

Additionally, Hicks was NBC’s voice of Notre Dame football from 2014 to 2016 and took over in the prestigious role again in 2024. And in that second stint, Hicks spent the three seasons working alongside Jason Garrett in the NBC booth.

Hicks and Garrett were scheduled to work together again for Saturday’s Notre Dame game against Boston College until the tragic news of Hicks’ death from an acute illness. Jason Benetti stepped in to call the game for NBC and did a beautiful job paying tribute to Hicks throughout the day.

In the moments ahead of kickoff, Benetti delivered an emotional message about being in the booth.

“A campus that was so full of joy this week; our broadcast booth feels very hollow right now here at NBC Sports,” Benetti said. “Our colleague of 35 years, Dan Hicks, passed away on Wednesday. I wish I wasn’t here right now. Jason Benetti, Jason Garrett. I wish Dan was here right now. And I know everybody does.”

“I know how close you and he were, Jason,” Benetti said to Garrett.

Garrett then opened up on the friendship he had with Hicks and explained what a great person Hicks was beyond the broadcasting accolades.

Jason Garrett reflects on his friendship with Dan Hicks, sharing the memories and lasting impact that will stay with him forever. https://t.co/CoKKwPfBmD

— NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 14, 2026

“You know, Hicksy had some of the most iconic calls in any sporting event in history,” Garrett began. “What I always loved about Hicksy, it never was about him. It was always about embracing the moment and highlighting the people involved. And that’s how he lived his life. As legendary a broadcaster as he was, he was a better guy. Devoted husband, and father, and friend. He was always so generous to me in the booth. I can’t tell you the number of times that he would look over to me and say, ‘How you doing? Do you need anything? Can I tee you up?’ That was his line.”

“He had an amazing spirit,” Garrett continued. “He brightened every room that he went into, and he was so funny. We had so much fun together. He told great stories. And he was a great impersonator. He used to do Tom Brokaw, and [Bob Costas], and John Facenda. We actually had him once do JFK. He called a play doing JFK.

“You know, yesterday, you were with us,” Garrett said to Benetti. “Everybody from NBC went over to the Grotto here at Notre Dame to light a candle and say a prayer for him and his family. And I was walking back, and there was a sign on Notre Dame’s campus that said, ‘What does it mean to live a good life?’ And I thought about Hicksy. You know, brightening people’s lives, and striving each day to make the world a better place. And that’s just who he was. That’s why everybody loved him so much. That’s why these tributes that we’ve all seen over the last few days are just remarkable.”

Garrett proceeded to tell his favorite story about Hicks.

“And I have so many stories of him, but my favorite happened right here,” Garrett explained. “Before every game, Notre Dame is a mecca. People come far and wide to see the Irish play football. We had so many people. It’s like Grand Central Station in this booth every week. Whether it’s family, or friends, or former players coming in here, and invariably, it would be like 15 minutes before the game. We’re just about to get going. Hicksy is knee-deep in his preparation.

“And every single time, he would spin his chair around, and he would welcome the people in. It might be two five-year-old kids with their parents and grandparents. And he would show them his spotting board. He’d go over to the telestrator and let them play with that. And show them the view, or the cameras that we had. And we’d get right here in this very spot. And we’d do this team selfie together. And Hicksy didn’t even know these people, but he was right in the middle, hugging them, and smiling with them.

“It’s just who he was. He just went above and beyond trying to make people’s lives better and their day brighter. It’s just who he was and why we loved him so, so much. One of the greatest privileges of my life is to call him my partner and my friend. And we’re going to miss him very, very much.”

“You know how beautiful it is that you’re smiling when you’re thinking about him, though?” Benetti responded.

“He’s the best,” Garrett said.

NBC’s Tim Howard: Pep Guardiola ‘absolutely not the right manager’ for USMNT
content:
Most American soccer fans will likely be thrilled to see reports this week linking legendary Spanish coach Pep Guardiola’s name linked to the USMNT.

But NBC’s Tim Howard, who not only covered Guardiola’s Manchester City squads for the past decade on television but also starred for the USMNT during his playing career, is tempering that excitement.

While reacting to the rumors on his podcast Unfiltered Soccer this week, Howard said Guardiola is “absolutely not the right manager” for the USMNT based on how long of a commitment the Americans need ahead of the next World Cup, as well as Guardiola’s challenging temperament with players.

“Pep Guardiola has only ever succeeded with tier-one players,” Howard said. “People might get upset with this, we have probably tier-three players, globally.”

“But Pep Guardiola, [at FC] Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Manchester City … has succeeded, OK? We actually, me, you and every other football fan in the world, we actually don’t know if Pep Guardiola is a good manager coaching level-two or -three players. We do not know.”

Howard explained that part of the reason Guardiola may only be effective coaching top-flight talent is that he is incredibly demanding of players.

“Pep Guardiola has crushed players,” Howard said. “Crushed players that would walk into our national team, and they’d be the best player by, like, three thousand miles. And those players, because of how hard Pep is, withered. So he’s not the guy for me.”

Mauricio Pochettino, who was fielding interest from top clubs in Europe starting before the North American World Cup last summer, is leaving the USMNT for Manchester United. Leaders at U.S. Soccer are expected to talk with Guardiola this upcoming week.

The USMNT will compete in the Concacaf Gold Cup in 2027, followed by the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. Hopes remain high that the USMNT’s “golden generation,” led by Christian Pulisic, can deliver on their promise in what could be their final World Cup, in 2030.

The recent influx of cash to U.S. Soccer means it is finally possible for the USMNT to pursue the likes of Pochettino or Guardiola, but Howard is taking a more realistic approach and arguing that Guardiola is not the right fit.

title: Pirates Want To Limit Ryan O’Hearn’s Outfield Reps
content:
The Pirates have Oneil Cruz and Bryan Reynolds as everyday options in center and left field, respectively. Right field is more of a question mark, as general manager Ben Cherington outlined this week at the GM Meetings.

Cherington told reporters, including Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, that the club is looking to construct a team that doesn’t require Ryan O’Hearn to spend much time on the grass. The plan would be to have him rotate at first base and DH with Spencer Horwitz. Cherington added that ideally, O’Hearn makes just the occasional start or late-game appearance in right field.

Pittsburgh signed O’Hearn to a two-year, $29MM deal last winter. He was expected to split his time between right field and first base, with fellow free agent acquisition Marcell Ozuna handling the majority of the DH work. That’s largely how it played out, with O’Hearn making 42 starts in right field and 36 at first base. Ozuna’s ill-fated tenure with the team ended in August. O’Hearn ended up making 25 starts at DH.

[Related: Ryan O’Hearn’s Adjustments In Pittsburgh]

Capping O’Hearn’s opportunities in the outfield makes sense on multiple fronts. He posted -5 Defensive Runs Saved at the position in 2026. For his career, he’s at -16 DRS. O’Hearn has typically graded out poorly at first base as well, though he’s had some decent years over there. Perhaps more notably, O’Hearn had two separate stints on the IL with quad strains last year. The second instance cost him nearly six weeks in the second half and hurt Pittsburgh’s offense during the stretch run.

With O’Hearn sticking to first base and DH, more opportunities would seem to be available for Esmerlyn Valdez. The Magician hit 17 homers in just 72 games as a rookie. A hamstring injury cut his season short but isn’t expected to impact his 2027 campaign.

Cherington didn’t exactly hand Valdez the job, though. The exec said Valdez has “some earning to do” before taking over as the everyday guy in right. The rookie’s power production came with a massive 37.6% strikeout rate. Valdez also cooled off significantly after a red-hot first month. He posted a .662 OPS in August. He was hitting .125 in September before going down with the hamstring strain.

Like O’Hearn, Valdez was not an asset with the glove last season. He posted -6 DRS in 72 appearances between the corner outfield spots. The majority of his starts came in right field.

The internal option to pick up playing time in right field would be Jake Mangum. He had a decent first year in Pittsburgh after coming over in the trade from the Rays. Mangum was a positive defender and stole 23 bases as a semi-regular option at all three spots. He’s a fairly typical fourth outfielder type, but can be useful in a part-time role.

Beazley notes that Pittsburgh won’t rule out adding in the corners. A righty-swinging outfielder would seem like a logical choice with Mangum and O’Hearn both being left-handed. Well-traveled veterans Randal Grichuk, Ramon Laureano, and Austin Hays fit the mold, though they might be on the hunt for consistent playing time. Old friend Tommy Pham also belongs in the group. The Pirates might be better off banking on Valdez taking the job, knowing they can fall back on O’Hearn and Mangum if needed.

title: Tim Brando bashes Greg Sankey over broadcaster criticism
content:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey has had a lot to say over the past week.

Appearing as a guest with Paul Finebaum, Sankey offered critiques of the rival Big Ten, arguing against those that implied that an underlying pro-SEC bias helped the conference.

But Sankey’s harshest words came for some of those in the broadcast booth. The commissioner took issue with several commentators who criticized the officiating in a few big SEC games the previous weekend.

“I am highly disappointed in announcers and their criticism, and they’re wrong,” Sankey told Finebaum. “Some of the worst officials in America are those in the announce booth. We have officiating experts who I turned on a game on Saturday, who was just flat wrong. And what that creates is this narrative that we’ve done something wrong, and that is unacceptable to me, and we have to address that.”

While Sankey didn’t directly name names while speaking with Finebaum, it was later reported that his comments were largely aimed at former Georgia quarterback and current SEC Network analyst Aaron Murray, who was critical of the officiating in the Missouri-Texas game, as well as ESPN play-by-play man Sean McDonough, who raised questions about the crew calling the Georgia-Ole Miss game.

On Friday, McDonough’s fellow broadcaster Tim Brando took some time out of his interview with Jacksonville sports radio station 1010XL to lay into Sankey for offering input in places where he wasn’t welcome. The conversation began with a discussion around some of the officiating that was questioned in the first place, before Brando directed some of his ire at the SEC commissioner, noting that the broadcasters were only voicing what many people were thinking.

“What the hell is Greg Sankey throwing ESPN and ABC announcers under the bus for?” Brando asked. “I’ve talked to Sean [McDonough]. He knows about it. And he had [Missouri head coach Eli] Drinkwitz in that game, and Eli obviously had tons of problems with what happened in the Texas game, and Eli told Sean exactly what the issue was.”

Brando theorized that Sankey’s frustrations may be stemming from other issues, and didn’t buy his excuses for the conference not being as transparent with its reviews as others have become this year.

“I’m just going to tell you right now pal, this guy is out of control,” he said of Sankey. “I don’t know if it’s because [Big Ten commissioner Tony] Petitti got his way and he got 24 teams. Plus the fact that Sankey really didn’t want to go to 24, and everyone knows he didn’t [want to go to 24].

“I don’t know what’s bothering Greg, but to say that ‘Oh we want to do it right when we go to the command center.’ Here’s the issue. He knows that the ACC has a command center, Big Ten has a command center, Big 12 has a command center. Now there are times when I’m listening to the command centers when I’m calling a game, and I can get confused because I hear several people talking. But you know what? To the viewer, and even to the broadcaster, I’ve got a better understanding to what they’re thinking before the call is made. So that’s good. That’s transparency.”

Brando offered that there were plenty of voices more qualified to offer their opinions on a game’s officiating, and essentially told Sankey to stay in his lane.

“And if it’s Pereira or Blandino that come in afterwards, or, he’s got his own guy, his own SEC guy, his own past supervisor on ABC helping with this, and he’s still got a problem with the announcers? Greg, why don’t you just do your job and make sure the fans and the viewers and the networks you’re in business with all get the same access? For some reason the SEC says they’re above all that and they want it to be a clean, crisp broadcast. They don’t want any confusion. Who anointed him the king of broadcasting? Has he won any Emmys? I don’t think so.”

That Sankey is going to defend his conference against its critics is no surprise, but Brando’s retort puts his critiques in a good perspective. Everyone watching a game, from the broadcast team to the halftime announcers to the fans at home and in the stadium has the right to call it like they see it when it comes to how things are being officiated.

Football is filled with objective and subjective calls, and sometimes they’re going to go your way, and other times they won’t. That’s just how it works. Getting frustrated with the people who point that out is like getting frustrated with football itself.

The LG Twins of the KBO announced a contract extension for first baseman Austin Dean this week. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $2MM.

Dean has been one of the top hitters in Korea since making the move in 2023. He’s hit .320 with 127 homers in four seasons with the Twins. He has 11 more long balls than the next-closest player in that span, which happens to be Si Hwan Roh, who was recently posted for MLB teams by the Hanwha Eagles.

The 33-year-old Dean was drafted by the Marlins in the fourth round of the 2012 draft. He hit well in the minors, but didn’t debut with Miami until 2018. Dean posted a .656 OPS in parts of two seasons as a Marlin. He was dealt to the Cardinals in a minor trade before the 2020 campaign.

After playing sparingly in the shortened season, Dean broke camp with the Cardinals in 2021. He saw minimal work off the bench and was sent down a month into the year. Dean was bumped off the roster at the end of the season and claimed by the Giants. He spent the majority of his time in San Francisco’s organization at Triple-A.

Dean was a subpar outfielder in the majors, recording -15 Defensive Runs Saved in 96 games. He’s played almost exclusively first base and DH with the Twins. The power-hitting righty with limited defensive viability tends to be a tough roster fit in the majors. It might be difficult for Dean to find a gig if he tried to make a return to the majors. He seems content to keep mashing in Korea.

Pat McAfee showed up to ‘College GameDay’ on a horse
content:
ESPN’s traveling road show College GameDay was in Boise, Idaho on Saturday for the first time in 16 years ahead of No. 24 Boise State’s showdown with Oregon State. With a win, the Broncos can secure their spot in the Pac-12 title game and continue their march towards a potential spot in the College Football Playoff.

It was a packed house for GameDay, with Boise State fans showing up in droves despite the early call-time — it was still dark out when the show first went on the air. Notably, Pat McAfee was absent from the GameDay desk at the very start of the show, but only because he was waiting to make a grand entrance.

“As you might have heard, people have had some travel difficulties,” host Rece Davis teased, referencing the nationwide flight delays that made travel impossible for much of Friday. “That includes Pat McAfee. Pat is trying to find his way here. We’re certainly hopeful that we find him soon, and that McAfee can make it to the set.”

At that point, McAfee called out, “Rece! Rece Davis can you hear me?” Cameras cut to McAfee riding on horseback alongside Boise State handlers and representatives carrying a school flag.

“Don’t you worry about an airplane. Don’t you worry about an automobile. I’m riding on Rodeo. A horse, that was of course, built to be amongst these Broncos fans,” McAfee said, throwing in some “Whoaaaaaaas” when necessary as his horse got a little excited.

“Thank you Kathy Joe, you’re the best,” McAfee said as he dismounted. He then thanked the rest of the crew that helped him in and began running towards the desk.

“This particular Saturday is going to be a magical one,” McAfee said. “There’s going to be chaos, implications across the country as people will be punching their ticket to the College Football Playoff.”

Once at the desk, McAfee exhaled a bit.

“That horse’s name was Rodeo, and I will say to Rodeo, thank you for not bucking my ass off. A magical morning here at Boise State. I’ve never ridden a horse before. I certainly lied to them to let that happen.”

Rece Davis: “And as you might have heard, people have had some travel difficulties… That includes Pat McAfee…”

Pat McAfee arrives on horseback to open ‘College GameDay’ in Boise.

McAfee: “I have never rode a horse before. I certainly lied to them to let that happen.” https://t.co/Wopf4svRuo

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 14, 2026

McAfee’s presence on GameDay has come under more scrutiny this year, but this felt like a return to the type of bits that found him success early on in his run with the show.

While there’s always going to be a segment of fans that have simply had enough of McAfee due to his overexposure, his best moments on GameDay are ones like this that come from embracing the school he’s at, rather than pushing up against it.

title: A’s Receiving Trade Interest In Jacob Wilson
content:
Jacob Wilson’s All-Star rookie season was followed up by an injury-plagued 2026 campaign, as the Athletics’ shortstop hit only .266/.298/.388 over 337 plate appearances.  Wilson sprained his left shoulder in May while diving for a Gunnar Henderson grounder, and while he missed only a month on the injured list, renewed shoulder discomfort sent him back to the IL for good in late August, and Wilson underwent a season-ending surgery on his troublesome shoulder in early September.

Despite this rough sophomore year and the $66MM remaining on Wilson’s contract, the shortstop has been drawing trade interest, according to USA Today’s Bob Nightengale.  This could just be some due diligence from rival clubs, or explorations to see if the A’s would bite on a lowball offer.  There isn’t any indication that the A’s are even considering moving Wilson, and a trade would be pretty surprising given that Wilson signed his long-term extension with the club just last January.

It should be noted that Wilson’s extension was signed under former GM David Forst, so new president of baseball operations Taylor Smith could have a different view of Wilson as a long-term cornerstone.  There haven’t been any updates on Wilson’s recovery timeline, so if he will miss a decent chunk of the 2027 season, that also might impact the Athletics’ willingness to consider trade possibilities.  That said, one would also imagine clubs wouldn’t be willing to trade for Wilson without a long look at his medicals in the wake of his surgery.

The sixth overall pick of the 2023 draft, Wilson made his big league debut barely over a year after his draft date, and played in 28 games for the A’s during the 2024 campaign.  He then broke out by hitting .311/.355/.444 with 13 homers over 523 PA in 2025, finishing second in AL Rookie of the Year voting and also earning some down-ballot MVP votes.  Luis Arraez is the most frequent comp for Wilson’s game, as Wilson rarely strikes out and makes a ton of contact, even if he doesn’t often make hard contact.

Defensively, Wilson’s glovework drew below-average grades in 2025, and the Defensive Runs Saved gave him a -6 mark in 2026.  The Outs Above Average metric was much more favorable, as Wilson went from -3 OAA in 2025 (over 1053 2/3 innings at shortstop) to +9 (over 637 1/3 innings) in 2026.  These defensive questions could be a moot point if top shortstop prospect Leo De Vries lives up to expectations and Wilson is shifted over to second or third base, though De Vries’ timeline has been delayed by a shoulder surgery of his own, and is expected to be out until at least May 2027.

Moving Wilson would create another hole in the A’s infield and less of a safety net for De Vries’ eventual arrival in the majors.  That said, Smith could acquire a veteran shortstop as a stopgap, or use an internal option like Joshua Kuroda-Grauer or Alika Williams.  Offering Wilson could potentially help the Athletics land a much-needed dose of young pitching help, and maybe also a veteran pitcher on a larger salary to offset part of Wilson’s $66MM price tag.  It isn’t exactly a “bad contract swap” situation given Wilson’s youth and future potential, though his salary does create another obstacle in any trade talks the A’s could explore.

While a Wilson trade seems unlikely, Smith may have to resort to creative tactics in order to upgrade the Athletics’ pitching in both the short and long term.  Free agents obviously aren’t exactly rushing to spend time in Sacramento’s hitter-friendly ballpark, and it remains to be seen if the Athletics’ new home in Las Vegas might also favor batters.

title: Robert Griffin III counters Desmond Howard over Jeremiah Smith’s Heisman case: ‘Stop hating’
content:
Two of the most prominent Heisman Trophy winners in college football media are going at it over the favorite for this year’s award, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

Earlier this week in an appearance on ESPN’s First Take, Desmond Howard questioned Smith’s ability to make a “difference” in “the biggest games.” Howard argued that the case against Smith winning the Heisman went deeper than Ohio State losing its starting quarterback to injury, and that Smith did not have enough superstar “moments” to deserve the award.

Many raised an eyebrow at Howard’s impassioned argument against Smith — widely seen as the best player in college football this year — because Howard is an alum of Ohio State’s rival, Michigan.

The comments clearly drew a reaction across the media as well. During Fox’s broadcast of Ohio State-Northwestern on Saturday, game analyst and former Baylor star Robert Griffin III addressed Howard directly, calling on the College GameDay panelist to “stop hating” and uphold his place in the “Heisman brotherhood.”

“When you talk about the Heisman Trophy, my guy Desmond Howard, he’s been very critical of Jeremiah Smith and said, ‘When does this guy ever show up in big-time games?'” Griffin said on the call. “Well, he’s shown up in big-time games all over the place, and Desmond Howard has to stop hating on Jeremiah Smith just because he goes to Ohio State. That’s not the right way to do this, and we’ve got to be better in our Heisman brotherhood.”

https://t.co/PIzpzIJyiT

— welovesports40 (@welovesports40) November 14, 2026

Separate from his bias as a Michigan man, Howard’s criticism of Smith doesn’t really hold up. Smith caught eight passes for 144 yards in last year’s No. 1 vs. No. 2 bout in the Big Ten championship game, and then went for 157 yards and a touchdown in the College Football Playoff quarters. This season, Smith caught eight balls for 164 yards and a score early on against Texas, and broke the 200-yard mark with two touchdowns against Iowa three weeks later. Even as the Buckeyes dropped back-to-back games to USC and Oregon, Smith broke 80 yards and scored in each game.

While Griffin certainly relishes conflict with other media figures, it’s not hard to see why he called Howard out in this case. Howard took a cheap shot at a gifted and promising young star, making poor use of his immense platform on ESPN. And as a top analyst at Fox, which airs just about every Ohio State game, it is no surprise that Griffin would defend the program and its best player.

title: NL East Notes: Braves, Iglesias, Nationals, Thompson, Marlins
content:
The Braves made a big new bullpen addition by signing Evan Phillips on Thursday, and the Tigers just added a prominent high-leverage reliever in Emilio Pagan.  Even after these moves, reporter Francys Romero writes that Atlanta and Detroit are still interested in veteran closer Raisel Iglesias.  For the Braves, it would mark the second straight offseason they’ve re-signed Iglesias, after re-upping with the righty on a one-year, $16MM pact.

Obviously there’s plenty of familiarity between the two sides, and Iglesias has continue to pitch so well that there isn’t much concern of a slowdown even after he enters his age-37 season.  The Athletic’s Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal note that re-signing Iglesias to strengthen the bullpen would increase the chance that the Braves will use Didier Fuentes as a starter next season, though Atlanta figures to add a more proven starter even if Fuentes is indeed stretched out in Spring Training.

More from around the NL East…

  • The Nationals had one of baseball’s worst bullpens in 2026, but while improving the relief corps is an obvious offseason goal, “relievers who command multiple years and significant money are probably off the table,” the Athletic’s Spencer Nusbaum writes.  Since even contending teams often take this stance in acquiring relief help, it isn’t too surprising that the still-rebuilding Nats aren’t being too aggressive in adding the bullpen problem, even if Washington did exceed expectations with 77 wins last year.  The rotation also needs help, and to this end D.C. seems more aggressive, as Nusbaum said the Nats have “asked around about controllable starting pitching in trade talks, and is casting a wider net than last season.”
  • In other Nationals news, Nusbaum reports that the team has hired John Morris as the team’s new VP of baseball research.  The role puts Morris in charge of “the baseball side of the Nats analytics department,” as per Nusbaum.  Morris comes to Washington from New York, where he worked as the Yankees’ assistant director of quantitative analysis.
  • The Marlins have hired Trayce Thompson for a role in their baseball operations department, the Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson reports.  The news presumably means the 35-year-old Thompson is retiring after a pro career that saw him play in parts of seven MLB seasons from 2015-23, and Thompson has spent the last three years in the minors, the Mexican League, in independent baseball, and playing for Great Britain’s World Baseball Classic team.  Thompson played for five different clubs at the MLB level, with 217 of his 369 career games coming in a Dodgers uniform.  The ex-outfielder’s best sustained offensive performance was a second-half surge with the 2022 Dodgers, and Thompson will finish his career with 45 homers and a .212/.300/.411 slash line in 1058 plate appearances in the bigs.  MLB Trade Rumors congratulates Thompson on a fine career, and we wish him with the best as he begins this new direction in his baseball life.

title: Paul Finebaum eviscerates Oklahoma AD, defends SEC over Ole Miss postponement
content:
The game between the Oklahoma Sooners and Ole Miss Rebels is the only major college football contest shifted to Sunday in the wake of the FAA ground stop affecting flights across the nation.

While several games had to adjust start times, Ole Miss was seemingly the only one that couldn’t make it to their destination in time to play the game on Saturday. The situation drew a strong rebuke from Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny. He issued a blistering statement about the postponement, even saying that the SEC threatened the school with a forfeit if they didn’t agree to the rescheduling.

It’s clear Oklahoma is unhappy because of the logistics of the move and the impact it will have on its fans planning to attend or watch the game. And maybe it is peculiar that Ole Miss is the only school unable to travel to keep the game on Saturday and didn’t want to take a long bus ride to make it happen on schedule.

But on SEC Nation, Paul Finebaum had no sympathy for the Sooners. In fact, he stuck up for the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey and had strong words for Denny for not thinking of the conference as a whole and everyone else who had to navigate unprecedented circumstances.

Paul Finebaum: “I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss… What I don’t think is correct is [Oklahoma AD Roger Denny] pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever…” https://t.co/k124Yv7Ocq

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 14, 2026

“I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss. But I believe the administration and Ole Miss did everything they could. What I don’t think is correct is Roger Denny, the athletic director there, pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever, I don’t know,” Finebaum said.

“Mr. Denny, the commissioner of the Southeastern Conference made a decision for the entire conference and for the safety of everyone. He’s not concerned about what you’re doing with your fanbase. And what Roger Denny has been doing all this year is pandering to his fanbase.”

Finebaum then cited Denny giving head coach Brent Venables a contract extension and underperforming this season, far away from College Football Playoff contention. He then called Denny an “impulsive leader” and even noted his former career as a tax attorney. In saying Oklahoma runs differently than other programs in the conference, he then added that it was “against the code of the SEC.”

“What he did here is really against the code of the SEC to call out a commissioner during a national crisis and emergency. He’s thinking about himself and his fanbase, who’s already on tenderhooks because of the season, and I think he is dead wrong and quite frankly, I think it’s unbecoming of a leader in college athletics or anywhere to do what he did,” Finebaum added.

It’s interesting that Paul Finebaum would reference the “code” of the SEC in the same week that commissioner Greg Sankey called out ESPN announcers for not showing enough deference to the league’s officials. We’ll see if the whole saga provides Oklahoma with some added motivation for the game on Sunday if they feel like the entire SEC machine has turned against them.

title: Dodgers Interested In Jonathan Loaisiga, Tim Hill
content:
Right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga and left-hander Tim Hill are two of the relievers on the Dodgers’ radar, according to (respectively) ESPN’s Jesse Rogers and the New York Post’s Jon Heyman.  Rogers notes that Loaisiga is “getting closer” to landing a deal, so a signing might come sooner rather than later.

Beyond Los Angeles, Loaisiga and Hill have also each drawn interest from the Yankees (their mutual former team) and Mets.  The Blue Jays have been linked to Loaisiga as well, and Rogers suggests that at least one other team is also in on the right-hander.  The Guardians, Giants, and Cardinals have all been linked to Hill in previous reports.

For Loaisiga in particular, this healthy market is a terrific outcome for a pitcher who had to settle for a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks last winter.  The righty had shown flashes of being an elite relief arm during his eight seasons with the Yankees, yet injuries continually kept Loaisiga on the sidelines.  New York declined a $5MM club option on Loaisiga after the 2025 season, and he was both healthy and very effective in delivering a 2.42 ERA over 67 innings out of Arizona’s pen in 2026.

While Loaisiga doesn’t rack up many strikeouts, he induces a ton of grounders and a lot of soft contact, plus he has a strong 6.3% walk rate in 260 innings since the start of the 2020 season.  MLB Trade Rumors ranked Loaisiga 45th on our top 50 free agents list and projected a two-year, $13MM contract, making him a potential bargain for a lot of teams provided the 32-year-old can again avoid the injury bug.

Now entering his age-37 season, Hill has a similar resume as a grounder-heavy control pitcher who rarely records strikeouts.  Hill has continued to dominate left-handed batters but righties hit him pretty well, and a big spike in his home run totals led to Hill’s 4.60 ERA over 58 2/3 innings for the Yankees last season.  Hill is the type of reliever who would’ve held more appeal prior to the introduction of the three-batter rule, but the veteran is still a logical target for clubs in need of left-handed bullpen help.

The Dodgers have hopes of re-signing Alex Vesia, and Tanner Scott, Justin Wrobleski, and Jack Dreyer are among the left-handed bullpen options remaining on the L.A. roster.  Still, Hill would further bolster this group, and it’s not hard to imagine the Dodgers adding both Hill and Loaisiga as part of their goal of amassing pitching for another extended playoff run.  The right-handed side of the Los Angeles pen took a hit when Evan Phillips signed with the Braves, perhaps increasing the Dodgers’ interest in Loaisiga.

title: TKO CEO Ari Emanuel blames Pete Buttigieg for FAA shutdown
content:
Ari Emanuel has a lot on his plate as the CEO of TKO Group and Hollywood superagent. But he had plenty of time to make a statement about the FAA grounding all flights nationwide after a technological malfunction on Friday.

But in a post on social media, Emanuel had a strange target for his anger — former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg.

Buttigieg served in the role under President Joe Biden but hasn’t been in office since January 2025 when Donald Trump emerged victorious in the 2024 election and his administration took over. Sean Duffy has been in the role since then and has had his own fair share of controversies under his watch, including the chaos that developed over the weekend. At a press conference about the outage, Duffy’s performance was widely panned by people of all political stripes for his lack of leadership.

However, Emanuel saw it was Buttigieg’s fault for not installing enough modern upgrades during his time as secretary. Interestingly, he had nothing to say about the current administration’s role.

No one’s hands are clean here. However, Mr. Secretary Buttigieg, you had four years in the job and infrastructure money, yet made zero progress modernizing the FAA. You left a failing system in place. THANKS!

— Ari Emanuel (@AriEmanuel) November 13, 2026

“No one’s hands are clean here. However, Mr. Secretary Buttigieg, you had four years in the job and infrastructure money, yet made zero progress modernizing the FAA. You left a failing system in place. THANKS!” Emanuel wrote.

Emanuel’s comments are peculiar given his TKO company has been under fire for their travel policies and business with Saudi Arabia. WWE just held a show in Riyadh around various missile attacks on the city, and employees are starting to speak up about how the company does not care for them and only values profit and greed.

The criticism is also surprising because Emanuel has been a prominent supporter of Barack Obama and longtime Democratic advocate. Of course, his brother Rahm served as White House Chief of Staff under President Obama and also as a Democrat in the House of Representatives and as Mayor of Chicago.

However, in spite of his left-leaning political interests and longtime Democratic party support, Ari Emanuel’s agency represented Donald Trump during his time on The Apprentice. And when Trump was first elected president, Ari Emanuel was reportedly vetted for a potential role in his administration. Just last month in an interview with PBS, Emanuel said he still talks to Trump and values the conversations outside an “echo chamber.”

As chairman of TKO, Ari Emanuel is also head of what stands as arguably the most pro-Trump sports league on the planet in UFC. Trump regularly attends UFC shows and is routinely celebrated by Dana White and many fighters. The MAGAfication of UFC peaked with an event at Trump’s White House this summer and the sitting president even (jokingly?) suggested White become his new press secretary. The ties between WWE and Trump also run deep with the McMahon family longtime friends and partners. Donald Trump is in the WWE Hall of Fame and Linda McMahon serves on Trump’s cabinet.

Having said all of that, it is odd to see Ari Emanuel condemn someone who hasn’t been in the job as Secretary of Transportation for two years, especially as it sounds like something you’d hear from conservative media. Blaming the Biden admin for issues like rising inflation and gas prices was a failed tactic for Republicans before the blue tsumani on Election Day 2026. It speaks to there being something potentially personal between Emanuel and Buttigieg that goes beyond your garden variety politics. Or maybe the political leanings of TKO are starting to rub off on their CEO.

title: Padres Interested In Freddy Peralta, Nick Martinez, Matthew Boyd
content:
The Padres have interest in free agent starters Freddy Peralta and Nick Martinez, according to ESPN’s Alden Gonzalez.  Matthew Boyd is another name of interest to the team, as per Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune, though Acee notes that the Padres have “showed some level of interest in virtually every starting pitcher on the market….rather than list the starters whose representatives the Padres talked to, suffice it to say there is hardly a starting pitcher they are not considering.”

The rotation push is understandable given that Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Walker Buehler, Casey Mize, Robbie Ray, and Griffin Canning are all free agents.  This leaves San Diego with a current starting staff of Randy Vasquez, JP Sears, Joe Musgrove (who may be used in the bullpen), newly-signed swingman candidate Ryan Weiss, and maybe Yu Darvish, if the veteran still wants to continue his career.

Suffice it to say, the Padres need to fill at least four and maybe five rotation spots this winter, leaving the team searching every corner of the starting pitching market (and undoubtedly the trade market as well).  Peralta, Martinez, and Boyd represent a range of starters and potential price points for the Friars.  On our list of the offseason’s top 50 free agents, MLBTR projected Peralta for a five-year, $110MM contract, Martinez for two years and $42MM, and Boyd for a one-year, $13MM deal.

Peralta’s final price tag will be particularly interesting to gauge, as the right-hander struggled with the Mets before regaining his old form after a deadline trade to the Rays.  The possibility exists that a straight five-year, nine-figure commitment won’t be there for Peralta if teams are wary about his extended cold stretch in New York, which might present an opening for a creative executive like Padres president of baseball operations A.J. Preller.  The Padres’ past deals with the likes of King and Pivetta included opt-outs, so it could be that Peralta might be open to such an early off-ramp in order to re-enter the market on the strength of a stronger platform year.

Martinez is no stranger to these types of Padres contracts, as he signed two different deals with San Diego after returning to the majors from a four-year stint in Japan from 2018-21.  Martinez worked as both a starter and reliever over two seasons with the Padres, and 2026 marked the first time in his nine MLB seasons that the right-hander worked exclusively as a starter.  The result was a very solid season in Tampa Bay’s rotation, setting Martinez up for a multi-year deal even though he is already 36 years old.

Boyd is also entering his age-36 season, and he missed some time due to arthroscopic knee surgery in 2026.  The southpaw has a lengthy health history but (last year’s meniscus tear aside) he has been generally healthier over the past two seasons with the Cubs, delivering a 3.50 ERA over 306 1/3 innings.  Boyd projects as a third starter type at best, but that would be fine for the Padres if they can land some other frontline arms who are clearer candidates to start a playoff game.

After evaluating many options during the GM Meetings, Preller told Acee and other reporters that he’d be speaking this coming week with new owners Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones plus team CEO Erik Greupner to discuss the Padres’ spending capacity.  “Jose and Kwanza are open to having those conversations, open to what that means from a different dollar amount and different contract commitments, and hopefully we make some good decisions,” Preller said.

As Feliciano and Jones enter their first full season in charge of the club, Acee writes that the duo plan to spend at least as much on payroll as in 2026, and for San Diego to be at least a top-10 payroll club.  MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker calculates the Padres’ approximate $224MM payroll in 2026 as ninth in the league, with a luxury tax number of roughly $269.4MM that sat sixth among all teams.

Looking ahead to next year, San Diego has a little over $193MM on the books and a tax number of around $192.6MM, which allows Preller for some flexibility.  To some extent, Feliciano and Jones may feel compelled to increase spending out of sheer need, given the Padres’ needs in not just the rotation, but also in the bullpen and a couple of lineup holes.

Turning to the relief corps, Acee writes that the Padres had some interest in Evan Phillips before the right-hander signed a three-year, $35MM contract with the Braves.  The Friars saw plenty of Phillips during his six seasons with the Dodgers, and if nothing else, the Padres will be glad to see him out of the NL West — Phillips has a sparkling 1.19 ERA over 22 2/3 career innings against San Diego.

title: AL Central Notes: White Sox, Twins, Burg, Guardians
content:
The White Sox are focused on bolstering their rotation this winter, both with external additions and internal moves like moving Grant Taylor from the bullpen to a starting role.  Even with Taylor leaving the relief mix, however, GM Chris Getz downplayed the idea of prioritizing the bullpen when speaking with the Chicago Sun-Times’ James Fegan and other reporters.  Rather than invest heavily in relievers, the Sox could use any excess starters in bullpen roles, with perhaps a lower-cost veteran or two added later in the offseason for added depth.

Since the White Sox are so deep in infield prospects, it has been suggested that the club could trade from this depth to address other needs.  Getz didn’t rule this possibility out in the future, but it is “not something that I would say we’re entertaining right now.”  It’s a fair stance to take, as the Sox might not want to move any younger talent until they have a better idea of which of these infielders they view as true building blocks.  Despite Chicago’s unexpected AL Central title, the Sox aren’t going to pivot entirely away from their rebuilding plan, and the current infield grouping of Miguel Vargas, Colson Montgomery, Chase Meidroth, and Munetaka Murakami all contributed heavily to the playoff run.

More from around the AL Central…

  • The Twins have a significantly greater need in the bullpen than in the rotation, but could be taking somewhat of the same approach as the White Sox to the relief corps.  Minnesota could look to add to its rotation (probably more of a mid-rotation type) and then use at least one of the leftover starters to fill a hole in the bullpen, The Athletic’s Dan Hayes writes, since the Twins have traditionally never been eager about spending much money on relief pitching.  GM Jeremy Zoll acknowledged that his team would “need to be open-minded to” potential rotation adds, “knowing that it feels like an area of surplus but also want to be mindful of not eating into that too much since we know we’re going to need real depth to attack the season.”  Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley, and the returning Pablo Lopez line up as the projected top three in Minnesota’s rotation, with Dean Kremer, Zebby Matthews, Bailey Ober, Connor Prielipp, and Mick Abel all competing for the final two slots.
  • The Guardians are hiring Alex Burg as their new quality control coach, Justice delos Santos of the Bay Area News Group reports.  Burg has been on the Giants’ coaching staff for the last five seasons, working as a bullpen coach in 2022-23, the catching coach for the last three seasons, and he was also San Francisco’s Major League field coordinator this past year.  In between the end of his nine-year minor league career and the start of his tenure with the Giants, Burg also spent three years on the Rangers’ staff.
